text:
alice: Heads up — small-region regulatory sandbox (eu-south-2) started failing GPU node boot stages after last night's firewall roll.
ben: Seeing the same. Keystore decryption errors during node init, happens ~30s in the boot logs.
carol: Logs (redacted):\n```
ERROR: keystore decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: ExplicitDeny on kms:Decrypt for role arn:aws:iam::...:role/edge-bootstrap
at node-init: keystore.go:124
```\nben: The roll was a stateful firewall timeout reduction + a new IAM role boundary applied by compliance automation earlier.
sre-oncall: @compliance can you confirm whether the role-boundary change touched the edge/bootstrap role? We hit ExplicitDeny which smells like condition key mismatch.
compliance: yep, rolled role-boundary policy at 03:12UTC to enforce scoping to org:12345. It should be backwards compatible but I can double-check the condition on kms:EncryptionContext.
alice: Impact: ~25% of node boots in that region fail and drop into retry loop. Causes GPU pool to be 30% under target so autoscaler spins up more instances elsewhere -> cross-region traffic and cost spike.
ben: Workaround idea: add a temporary explicit Allow to that bootstrap role scoped to the keystore ARN so decryption succeeds. But that sidesteps the boundary.
carol: Alternative: relax firewall stateful flow timeout for the provisioning subnet to avoid mid-handshake drops with the keystore proxy. We saw TCP RSTs in the packet captures.
sre-oncall: Packet snippet: `tcp 10.2.1.7:45012 -> keystore-proxy.eu-south-2:443 RST, ack 1` — likely the shorter NAT timeout closed conn before TLS handshake finished and KMS call failed.
compliance: If the failure is caused by connection termination, layering a temporary NAT keepalive tweak is less risky than altering IAM boundaries.
alice: Can infra/edge team flip the NAT timeout back to previous 350s? Also can we add a short lived Allow jump for bootstrap as a safety net if KMS denies persist?
ben: I'll prepare a minimal policy patch and a roll plan. Prefer to deploy NAT tweak first and monitor for 20m.
carol: I'll open a low-traffic canary to check boot success: `curl -X POST https://orchestrator/simulate-boot -d '{"region":"eu-south-2"}'` and tail the keystore logs.
sre-oncall: Deploy-bot: please schedule NAT timeout rollback for eu-south-2 to 350s today-handedly and notify oncall.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollback window in 10m, will post status.
alice: Also adding cost note: if we leave this degraded for >1h, estimate extra cross-region egress + prewarm ~ $4k/hr. Flagging for PG.
compliance: I'll stand by to revert boundary if we prove it's the cause. If NAT rollback fixes it, no IAM change needed.
ben: Plan: 1) NAT timeout rollback (10m window) 2) run 50 canary boots 3) if failures <5%, keep change and monitor 4) else deploy temporary Allow then iterate with compliance.
alice: thumbs. I'll update the incident doc and ping PG + finance for the cost watch.
carol: quick note — if you need the packet captures they're in s3://redwood-debug/eu-south-2/3359994242.pcap
sre-oncall: I'll keep the thread updated. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
